events.content:
I like to create a different personalized image of me and project that image to society. I like being unique and care and think about my image that I project to others. I also preserve beauty and aesthetics rather than tinker with something, I don't, at the first impression, try to tinker with things, I just love the concept of anything. I'm apt at interpreting by looking at the structure (eg. body Language, attire, positioning, environment, ambience etc.) (passive data) of something or someone but not necessarily the active data (words spoken, perspectives, graphs, numerical or categorical data). Also, I'm a highly impatient person. I do not like ambiguity. My grasping or interpreting ability of anything is very fast. When I get ideas or grasp anything, I want to implement them faster and get unstable because I don't want to lose them. Also I don't get ideas sitting at one place and resting but I get them while I'm in motion. My ideas are either a right train of thought suddenly appearing, or none and I don't get it. It's a hit or miss. I also have anxiety problems, am careful at not doing mistakes, so making my work perfectionistic. I'm very careful at doing my work right and making it perfect. I'm not a calm, collected person, as you can understand. But one thing is one, my inferring skills are those that seperate me from others. I'm a changing mindset person, one thing which looks well and good might not seem fair later. That's because of outside or external input. This suggests that my focus is external. As I said , I'm a passive data oriented person, eg.- I remember when I said where I said or when it happened where it happened than what I said or what happened. I'm a results driven and direct person and I can't do small talk. I start but can't take the conversation further, words don't come on the moment. Hence, I've fear talking to people (not comfortable with people). I largely improvise. I'm a person who prefers improvisation. I care about my image also. I don't have a good presence of mind and am not socially smart. I take time to handle things that's because of doing the thing perfectly and carefully in order to make it perfect and because of which I am sometimes perceived as slow in doing my work. I'm very intuitive. I am not tolerant of people doing mistakes. My inner self gets angry at those people. Ideas come on-the-go to me, not while I'm resting. I also don't like having the same experiences again. I hate the feeling. I crave for change. Can't stick to one thing for a long period of time. Don't like reading long writings that much, don't have the patience to read them because I like action.

Which career sounds like the best fit and stands out for me?

Based on the information you've provided, it seems that you are a creative, detail-oriented, and results-driven individual who values aesthetics, uniqueness, and personal image. You have excellent inferring skills and are able to interpret passive data effectively. You are also a quick learner and prefer to work on ideas that come to you spontaneously rather than sitting down and brainstorming. Additionally, you have a low tolerance for mistakes and prefer to work on tasks that allow you to improvise and be flexible.

Given these traits, a career in the creative field such as graphic design, fashion design, or interior design may be a good fit for you. These careers allow you to express your creativity and attention to detail while also allowing you to work on projects that require quick thinking and improvisation. Additionally, these careers often involve working with visual elements, which aligns with your preference for interpreting passive data.

Another potential career path could be in marketing or advertising, where your ability to interpret passive data and your focus on aesthetics and personal image could be valuable assets. You could work on creating visually appealing advertisements or marketing campaigns that effectively communicate a brand's message.

Alternatively, you may also consider a career in event planning or project management, where your ability to quickly grasp ideas and implement them efficiently would be highly valued. These careers also allow for a high degree of flexibility and improvisation, which aligns with your preference for working on-the-go.

Ultimately, the best career fit for you will depend on your specific interests, skills, and values. It may be helpful to explore different career paths and speak with professionals in those fields to gain a better understanding of what each career entails and whether it aligns with your strengths and preferences.
